CONAN live in Athens

Παρασκευή 6 Μαρτίου στις 20:00 | Gazarte

The riff crashes through the room before you've finished crossing the threshold. Gazarte's stage holds the particular weight of an international metal act about to unleash decades of fury. CONAN has arrived in Athens, and the venue is already vibrating with anticipation.

CONAN deals in doom — the kind that measures time in glacial riffs and bass frequencies that rearrange your internal organs. The band from Liverpool has built a reputation on music that moves slowly but hits like continental drift. Each song unfolds like a ritual, patience rewarded with moments where the full weight of the sound lands on your chest and refuses to lift.

The doom metal community operates by its own rules. The tempo runs slower than most metal subgenres, the riffs repeat and mutate, the vocals often sit buried in the mix like ancient incantations. CONAN pushes this approach to extremes — songs that stretch toward ten minutes, a guitar tone so thick it becomes geological. The initiated understand what they're receiving. The uninitiated either convert or retreat.

Gazarte's Ground Stage provides the acoustic containment this band requires. The low ceiling focuses the sound, walls becoming resonating chambers. When CONAN drops into their lowest registers, the room becomes an instrument — the floor transmitting frequencies the speakers can't fully reproduce.

The crowd arriving tonight carries the markers of the tribe. Band shirts trace lineages through doom, stoner, and sludge metal. Conversations before doors compare setlists from other cities on the tour. The anticipation has the quality of religious devotion — these are pilgrims who've waited years for this band to reach Athens.

Metal shows in Athens run on their own schedule. Expect support acts to set the tone before CONAN takes the stage later than posted. The bar serves efficiently between sets, but the dedicated claim spots near the stage and hold them. Movement during CONAN's set tends toward swaying rather than moshing — the tempo doesn't invite the usual pit dynamics.

If you need speed or variety in your metal, CONAN will test your patience. This is music that rewards surrender, that demands you abandon the expectation that something faster is coming. But if you've been waiting for doom that operates at the heaviest end of the spectrum, where the riff is everything and the riff takes its time — Gazarte holds what you need.

CONAN live — doom metal that measures time in tectonic movements, each riff a monument.
